Verified on candidate sha256:baa6ff4d... (source dab4562). (1) My own delayed-boot-/me probes (generated by scripts/gen-147-probes.py: one inserted page.route line that forwards the next GET /me, i.e. the boot /me of /about, 1.5 s or 4 s late, forcing the round-6 trace order: goto returns, re-login, then the boot /me). The pre-repair spec (1e0dc5d) fails 12/12 (2 delays x 3 repeats x en/ar) with exactly the round-6 failure 'Expected: 403 / Received: 200'; these 12 failures are by design (they reproduce the race). The candidate spec passes 12/12, including at a 4 s delay, so the wait is not a fixed sleep that a slower /me would outrun. (2) Contention: the candidate's 'a 403 is not a session end' x10 per project passed 20/20 at load 5-9 and 20/20 again with the load held at 13-17 (median 13.7). (3) It also passed in both full e2e runs (en and ar, locale unset at load up to 30, and C.UTF-8). (4) Diff review: the repair only adds the waitForResponse on the boot GET /me (asserted 200) and waits for the signed-in shell's sign-out button before the re-login; every later assertion (403 csrf, the not-saved notice in the chosen language, the live region, header layout, axe, watched.me - meAt <= 1) is unchanged. The shell wait is a real guard, because the sign-out button renders only from the /me answer that also stores the CSRF token.

Not closed on candidate sha256:baa6ff4d... (source dab4562). What the repair delivers, verified: (a) the root test script now runs unit-node, unit-web and unit-formula-nocodegen as three invocations, each run even when an earlier one fails, and still exits 1 on any failure: H3 (failing unit-node test), H4 (failing unit-web test) and H5b (a test failing ONLY under --disallow-code-generation-from-strings, at low load) each give EXIT 1 with all three invocations run (02h, 02h2); the no-codegen project ran in every one of my 12 pnpm test runs. (b) The warm-up does not change what a test asserts: it fills the module cache through import.meta.glob and never calls lazyPage's once()/load(), so router pages still render through React.lazy and Suspense; my probe shows a lazyPage over a WARMED module (re-import 0.1 ms) still renders the translated polite fallback first and the page afterwards (H1, 16/16), and a mutant that sets the Suspense fallback to null fails 4 tests with the warm-up active (H2), so the fallback is still exercised. The 5 s asyncUtilTimeout is unchanged. What the finding required and is NOT achieved: pnpm test reproducible at load >= 13, the load the concurrent reviews create (D-131 asked FE-R10 to show it at 13-16). Reproduction, same procedure as round 6, in a complete clone: (1) at the concurrent-review load (1-min load 7.7 rising to 22-30, 21:59-23:03Z) 3 of 4 runs exit 1: node22-unset and node22-C fail raid.test.tsx 'action register' (en), 'Unable to find role="link" and name "Synthetic call the vendor"' after the 5 s wait (6974 ms and 5426 ms; the first /actions render in the file, the page module already warmed); node24-unset fails apps/api/src/architecture.test.ts 'every import respects dependsOn...' at 33.4 s against its 30 s timeout. The three harness pnpm test runs H3-H5 at load 24-27 also each hit that architecture timeout (36.4, 40.8, 34.5 s). (2) With the load held by the round-6 controller (208 samples, median 14.39, p10-p90 12.40-16.82; during the failing run median 15.52, 12.40-17.65), node22-unset exits 1 with BOTH classes again: architecture.test.ts 41.1 s 'Test timed out in 30000ms', and raid 'action register' (en) at 5.3 s; the other three held runs exit 0. That load is inside FE-R10's own band (median 14.75-15.62); FE-R10's band was made of pure busy loops, mine also carried a concurrent Playwright e2e run, as the delivery process does. (3) At low load (2.1-5.5) 4/4 exit 0. So the repair improves the rate (round 6: 6/8 contended runs failed; here 4/8, plus 3/3 harness runs) but pnpm test still fails at load 13-16 and above, in both of the finding's classes: a first render of a page that misses the 5 s wait, and the architecture test that misses its 30 s timeout (FE-R10 itself recorded the 21.3 s of 30 s residual and left it to API scope). The product is unaffected: every failing test passes at low load. Severity stays Low (test-harness reproducibility). A fix would need to cover the architecture test's budget or work (API/solution-architect scope) and the first-render path under load, or a documented, justified load envelope for pnpm test as a gate check, as the finding's 'expected' allows.
